assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
Period analysed is 1 October 2026 to 31 October 2026, across all regions.
caveats: Success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level 89.2%, order-level 91.6%, technical 92.9%. Retries and drop-offs explain the gap.
On 12 October, 341 attempts were ingested twice; the duplicates were removed and each attempt is counted once.
Attempt volume was 39% above normal from 18 to 31 October. This may be a real event such as a sale or a data gap, so check before comparing totals across this period.

facts.text: The attempt success rate for 1-31 October 2026 is 89.2%, with 384,193 successful attempts out of 430,580 attempts.
Under other definitions the rate is higher: 91.6% at order level (384,192 of 419,385 orders) and 92.9% technical (384,193 of 413,684). The widest gap between definitions is 3.64pp.
On 12 October, 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts); these are counted once in the figures.
Attempt volume ran 39% above the usual level for those weekdays from 18 to 31 October (14 days).

response.headline: This month (October 2026) the attempt-level payment success rate is 89.2%: 384,193 successful attempts out of 430,580.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Compare the number of attempts per order and the share of orders that succeed on a retry after an earlier failed attempt.
hypotheses.rationale: Attempt-level counts every retry in the denominator, while the order-level rate counts each order once; the order-level denominator is smaller (419,385 vs 430,580).
hypotheses.text: The gap between the attempt-level rate (89.2%) and the order-level rate (91.6%) is likely driven by customers retrying failed payments, since each retry counts as a separate attempt.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the marketing/sales calendar for 18-31 October and compare with source system volumes.
hypotheses.rationale: Both real events and data gaps produce this kind of spike, so the evidence alone cannot distinguish them.
hypotheses.text: The late-October volume spike may be a sale or other business event rather than a data gap.

recommendations.rationale: The rate ranges from 89.2% to 92.9% depending on the denominator, so mixing definitions would give misleading comparisons.
recommendations.text: State which definition (attempt, order or technical) is being used whenever the success rate is quoted or compared.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The late-October volume spike may be a sale or other business event rather than a data gap.
recommendations.rationale: A 39% volume jump can shift mix and totals, and it is not yet confirmed whether it is a real business event.
recommendations.text: Confirm the cause of the 18-31 October volume spike before comparing this month's totals with other periods.
